updates.summary: People describe it as "eerie and elegant," which is the right non-spoilery sell. It moves like a ghost story but lands like a sorrowful folk nightmare full of atmosphere and longing.
updates.good_pick_if: you want horror that is graceful, eerie, and emotionally heavy
updates.maybe_skip_if: you want jump scares or a louder scare rhythm

updates.summary: One reviewer calls it "sensual nightmare suburbia," and that is almost unfairly accurate. It is funny, disturbing, and so committed to its mood that the whole movie feels like forbidden curiosity.
updates.good_pick_if: you want something stylish, weird, and genuinely unnerving
updates.maybe_skip_if: you want emotional safety or realism without menace

updates.summary: People love it as "expressionist insanity," which is really the fun of it. The sets are so warped and the mood so committed that it still feels like horror beamed in from another dimension.
updates.good_pick_if: you want a classic that still looks wild and feels uncanny
updates.maybe_skip_if: you want modern pacing or naturalistic performances

updates.summary: One review loves how it turns into "moral confrontation" instead of simple payback. It is beautiful, cold, and emotionally thorny in a way that keeps the revenge setup from feeling routine.
updates.good_pick_if: you want something intense, exacting, and morally messy
updates.maybe_skip_if: you want cleaner catharsis or less anguish

source_quotes.source: Letterboxd review by ARWIN EDWARD BAGASLAO

updates.summary: People call it "slyly nasty" for good reason. It is smooth, suspenseful Hitchcock fun where the tension comes from how casually the whole thing slides toward danger.
updates.good_pick_if: you want a clean, highly watchable thriller with old-school craft
updates.maybe_skip_if: you want messier psychology or modern brutality

updates.summary: One reviewer calls it "windblown hysteria," which is a great way to frame it. The landscape feels hostile, the emotions stay raw, and the whole movie has a fevered silent-era intensity.
updates.good_pick_if: you want something tense, elemental, and visually fierce
updates.maybe_skip_if: you want comfort or a softer romantic register

updates.summary: People describe it as "wound up so tightly," and that is absolutely the sensation. It is slick, nasty, and powered by a lead performance that makes ambition feel like a horror device.
updates.good_pick_if: you want something sharp, creepy, and relentlessly watchable
updates.maybe_skip_if: you want a moral center or less sociopathic energy

updates.summary: One review calls it "a nightmare you can't wake up from," which is exactly the lane. It is emotionally volcanic, physically wild, and closer to a full breakdown than to normal horror plotting.
updates.good_pick_if: you want something intense, deranged, and unlike anything else
updates.maybe_skip_if: you want coherence, calm, or emotional protection

source_quotes.text: A nightmare? yes, but one you can’t wake up from.

updates.summary: People keep calling it "slow-burn perfection," and that is the right expectation to set. It works through unease, class tension, and the feeling that every scene is hiding something just out of reach.
updates.good_pick_if: you want something atmospheric, smart, and built on ambiguity
updates.maybe_skip_if: you want quick answers or faster escalation

updates.summary: One good pitch calls it "beautifully grotesque," and that really is the attraction. It is lurid, theatrical, and surprisingly emotional underneath all the circus-from-hell imagery.
updates.good_pick_if: you want horror that is wild, visual, and emotionally off-kilter
updates.maybe_skip_if: you want restraint or less grotesque imagery
